blocks.text: I can understand the key themes and the characters’ emotions in ‘The Journey’.
You will find the big ideas in the story, then think about how the girl feels at different moments. This helps us get ready to write a diary entry as her.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A big idea, topic or message that appears in a story.
A person, being, thing or animal in a story.
Strong feelings that result from a person’s circumstances, mood, or relationship with others.
The ability to understand other people’s feelings and points of view.

blocks.text: Stories often have {themes} that communicate a deeper message to the reader. Here are some themes you might notice in different stories:

items: friendship
pride
good vs evil
family
resilience
celebration
suffering
grief
greed
hope

blocks.label: Do readers always agree?
blocks.text: No! Readers can interpret themes, and how important they are, differently.
‘The Journey’ conveys important messages through exploring four themes. Tap each one to see its meaning.

items.def: A violent dispute between states or nations.
Holding on to the belief that there will be a positive outcome.
The forced removal of a person from their home or country, often due to armed conflicts or natural disaster.

blocks.q: Match each theme to its meaning.

pairs.b: a violent dispute between states or nations
holding on to the belief that there will be a positive outcome
the forced removal of a person from their home or country

blocks.text: Think about the start of the story. How do the characters experience war and conflict?

items: Everything changed for the girl and her family as soon as the war began in her country.
Her mother now worries about her family more than ever.
They are feeling less positive and hopeful.

blocks.text: War and conflict had a very negative effect on the family. It made them worried and scared.
If you are {displaced}, you do not choose to leave your home. You are **forced** to leave.

items: The sisters didn’t want to leave, but they knew they had no choice.
It was horrible to say goodbye to their home.
A new place seems strange and scary, but feeling safe matters more than anything.

blocks.q: Which sentence about the family is true?
options: They were happy to be displaced
They were forced to leave, and did not want to go, but knew they had to stay safe
They chose to leave because they wanted an adventure
blocks.why: Displacement is being forced to leave your home. The girls did not want to go, but they knew their safety came first.

blocks.text: The journey was very challenging, but the family never gave up, even when they were really scared and tired.

items: Even when they are faced with a huge sea to cross, they don’t give up.
Their mother acts bravely, even though she is scared, to protect her daughters.
They stay strong and determined to reach safety.

blocks.text: {Resilience} means adapting to and withstanding difficulties. The family faced extreme hardship, but they remained strong.

blocks.q: What is the main way the family show resilience?
options: They keep travelling even when it is incredibly challenging
They stay at home and wait
They turn back at the first problem
blocks.why: Resilience is withstanding difficulties. The family carry on travelling even when it is very hard.

blocks.text: The theme of {hope} runs through the whole story. The characters try to overcome challenges and hold on to the belief that they can find a place of safety and build a new life.

blocks.label: Think about it
blocks.text: What would have happened if the family had given up hope? They might have gone back to their house, or maybe never have left at all.

blocks.label: Look closely at the birds
blocks.text: On the train, birds follow the family. They are also migrating to another country, but they do not have any difficulty crossing borders.

blocks.q: Choose the theme that fits each sentence.

items.q: The family were forced to pack up and leave home. This shows …
They keep going even when the sea crossing is scary and hard. This shows …
They believe they will find a place of safety in the end. This shows …
Their country is devastated by a violent dispute. This is …

blocks.text: When we write a diary entry as the girl, we need to understand her {perspective}, which is her point of view.
We do this with **empathy**: understanding and sharing the feelings of another. Empathy helps us think of the thoughts she would share in her diary.
Expressing thoughts and emotions is a key part of writing a diary entry.
The girl’s emotions change throughout the story. Here are the key events in order:

items: 1. A war begins in the country where the girls had been living happily with their mother and father.
2. After their father dies, their mother decides to flee their country to take them to a safer place.
3. At the border, they are banned from crossing and hide in the forest overnight.
4. They have a challenging ferry crossing over rough seas with fellow refugees.
5. They take a train through many countries and travel closer to a new, safe home.

blocks.text: At each key moment, we ask: what did she feel, and why?

slides.title: Start and end: how she might feel

blocks.text: At the beginning, she could write:

items: I don’t feel safe anymore.
Every day, I feel more and more scared.
How can everything change so suddenly?

blocks.text: By the end, she could write:

items: I am so relieved to be close to safety.
I am happy we are safe, but I still miss my home.
I hope there is a place we can go to play outside in peace.

blocks.label: What do you notice?
blocks.text: Her emotions change from **scared and worried** at the start to **relieved and hopeful** at the end, though she still misses home.

slides.title: Match the moment to the thought

blocks.q: Match each moment to a thought the girl might have had.

pairs.b: It breaks my heart to say goodbye to everybody.
I couldn’t sleep because I was so terrified.
I was desperate to get off the boat, my stomach was churning!

pairs.a: On the train, closer to safety
pairs.b: I hope we find a safe place soon.

flashcards.front: Name the four themes explored in ‘The Journey’.
flashcards.back: War and conflict, resilience, hope and displacement.

flashcards.back: A violent dispute between states or nations.

worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase. Think about the themes and the girl’s feelings in ‘The Journey’.

questions.prompt: What word means a big idea, topic or message that appears in a story?
questions.explanation: A theme is a big idea, topic or message that appears in a story.

questions.prompt: Which theme means adapting to and withstanding difficulties?
questions.explanation: Resilience is adapting to and withstanding difficulties.

questions.prompt: Which theme means holding on to the belief that there will be a positive outcome?
questions.explanation: Hope is holding on to the belief that there will be a positive outcome.

questions.prompt: Which theme means the forced removal of a person from their home or country?
questions.explanation: Displacement is being forced to leave your home or country.

questions.prompt: Which theme means a violent dispute between states or nations?
questions.explanation: War and conflict is a violent dispute between states or nations.

questions.prompt: Which word means the ability to understand and share the feelings of another?
questions.explanation: Empathy is understanding and sharing another person’s feelings.

questions.prompt: Which word means a person’s point of view?
questions.explanation: Perspective refers to a person’s point of view.

questions.prompt: Which word means strong feelings that result from a person’s circumstances, mood, or relationships?
questions.explanation: Emotions are strong feelings that result from someone’s circumstances, mood, or relationship with others.

questions.prompt: Which theme runs through the whole narrative of ‘The Journey’, as the family believe they will find a place of safety?
questions.explanation: The theme of hope runs through the whole story.
